about: The map's Status and Roadmap tabs (methodology.js) read this file. tests/test_roadmap.py fails when a file, switch or methodology part named here is gone, or when an evidence quote is no longer in the file it cites, so a change to the code or the ledger that makes an entry wrong fails CI. Update an item in the change that moves it; remove it when it is done (git and the PR keep the history).

measures.label: Reference roofs fully right
measures.detail: Latest round against the owner's drawings, built blind (round 0 was 8).

measures.label: Right even from the drawn lines
measures.detail: The drawn lines fed through the lines-to-faces step: the ceiling for any reader.

measures.label: Obstructions found that are real
measures.detail: On 195 drawn roofs; 45% of drawn obstructions are found.

measures.label: Panel count change from a 10 cm outline nudge
measures.detail: Why one roof's count is noisy.
measures.quote: panel count by a median of 26%

measures.label: Dark winter days, Cromwell
measures.detail: Days under a fifth of the year's average sunlight, May to July 2016-2025.

measures.label: Independent accuracy benchmark
measures.detail: Yield is compared with PVGIS, another model; geometry with one person's drawings.
measures.quote: There is no independent accuracy benchmark yet.

items.title: Station-corrected low-solar runs for Cromwell, Wānaka and Alexandra
items.why: Resilience counts dark days from ERA5 cells about 25 km across, which miss valley fog. Only the Wakatipu cells are corrected to a sunlight sensor on the map today, so battery days are understated elsewhere.
fix: Commit the multi-station correction and its sensor-shade audit
Publish the new climate/era5 files
Report the worst spell from the station record itself, since even the corrected series halves it

refs.how: What the sunlight data cannot see

items.title: Wānaka and Hāwea sunlight from their own sensor
items.why: Yearly sunlight comes from one Queenstown calibration spread with ERA5. Wānaka's sensor reads about 9% lower, so kWh and savings there are likely too high.
fix: Finish the station audit
Add the stations to NIWA_MEASURED_GHI_STATIONS
Rebuild (a sun-model change needs a full rebuild)

items.title: Fix the step that turns roof lines into faces
items.why: Even the owner's own drawn lines come out right on at most 76 of 100 roofs after this step, so it caps every reader. It needs no training data.
fix: Small faces and joins (about 24 roofs)
The roof edge from the roof map (about 10)
Straight lines (about 9)

evidence.quote: three converter stages each cost roofs with perfect input

items.title: A better roof reader, judged on the 100 reference roofs
items.why: 18 of 100 reference roofs come out fully right. Most have at least one missing or invented line, which puts panels across ridges and on the wrong face.
fix: Read large roofs in tiles (a 70 m roof at 384 px is 0.2 m a pixel)
Try a different reader model: more drawings of the same kind stopped helping
One round at a time against the 100, then the 30 held back

items.title: Hand-drawn roofs never dropped without a warning
items.why: One error handler around the drawn obstructions and fold lines skips them all if the label file fails to load, so drawn roofs would quietly lose their markup.
fix: Count and print every failure
Fail the build when drawn roofs lose their markup

items.title: Steadier panel counts on each roof
items.why: A 10 cm nudge to an outline moves a roof's panel count by a median 26%, so a single roof's count is noisy.
fix: Best of several small placements (LAYOUT_PERTURBATIONS_M): +3.45% panels, about twice the layout time
Screen the district for bad layouts and hold the worst

evidence.quote: panel count by a median of 26%

items.title: Find roofs built or changed since the 2021 laser scan
items.why: Heights come from the 2021 scan and the photos from 2026. A roof built since then has no real heights and can read as one flat face.
fix: Flag buildings where the photo and the scan disagree and let the photo reading lead
Count them
Take new LINZ scans as they are flown

refs.how: A laser scan of the roofs

items.title: Real pitch and roof form where there is no laser scan
items.why: Cromwell, Bannockburn, Glenorchy and Kinloch are built on a modelled surface with every house at one guessed pitch.
fix: Tell gables from hips from the photo
Pitch by building type

items.title: Obstructions from a trained photo model in every town
items.why: Fewer than half the obstructions found are real and fewer than half of the drawn ones are found. The colour detector draws most of the false area.
fix: Retrain the photo model with the reference roofs held out
Use it, or use it to check the others, where there is a laser scan

items.title: A likely range on every figure
items.why: There is no independent accuracy benchmark, so a card shows one number with no range. The known input errors (sunlight by town, panel-count noise, load and price assumptions) can be carried through to a low and high figure.
fix: Carry each input's measured spread through the workings to a range
Show the range on the card and in its workings
Compare sunlight with the NIWA stations and a second model (PVGIS, Himawari) in every town

evidence.quote: There is no independent accuracy benchmark yet.

items.title: A second set of drawn roofs outside Queenstown
items.why: Every drawn roof is in Queenstown and by one person, so accuracy elsewhere is unknown.
fix: Draw a stratified set in Wānaka, Cromwell and Arrowtown
A second person marks some of the same roofs

evidence.quote: There is no independent accuracy benchmark yet.

items.title: Hills that block skylight as well as direct sun
items.why: One monthly cloud factor puts most low-sun light in the diffuse part, which the far horizon does not cut. Winter output under big hills is probably too high.
fix: Daily direct and diffuse light from measured or satellite data
A sky-view factor for the diffuse part

items.title: Household use that varies day to day
items.why: A home's daily pattern comes from about 40 homes in another region in 2015, and average days likely overstate how much solar a home uses itself.
fix: Vary each day with the daily weather already loaded
Use smart-meter shapes from the Electricity Authority or a retailer

evidence.quote: about 40 homes in Taranaki and Hawke's Bay, 2015

items.title: Export limits, retail plans and grid charging
items.why: Export caps and network limits are not modelled, so savings on large systems are too high, and a battery charges only from solar.
fix: An export limit on the card
Pick a retail plan
Battery charging from the grid overnight

evidence.quote: Export limits, feed-in caps and network constraints.

items.title: Install cost that knows the building
items.why: Cost comes from a few per-kW bands. Height, access, scaffolding and switchboard work are not counted, so two-storey and complex roofs cost more than shown.
fix: A cost adder for storeys from the measured building height
Local installer quotes

items.title: Build keys that see a no-imagery run
items.why: A run without aerial imagery keeps the same build key, so a layout built with imagery can be kept under a run that has none.
fix: Put SOLAR_SELECTED_FACES and SOLAR_INCLUDE_IMAGERY in the reading hash

items.title: Build all of New Zealand
items.why: The map covers one district. The worker fleet has never run as a fleet, and any geometry change marks every building stale.
fix: Build keys per stage
A fleet rehearsal under the hour cap
A CPU quota increase

evidence.quote: has never run as a fleet
